candidates.name: Cappella Sansevero
candidates.content: A chapel built in 1590, it contains sculptures and other works of art by some of the leading Italian artists of the 18th century, like the extraordinary Veiled Christ by Giuseppe Sanmartino. It also has a high scientific interest

candidates.name: San Domenico Maggiore
candidates.content: One of the most prominent churches of Naples. This Gothic church (est. 1283) incorporates a smaller, original church built on this site in the 10th century, San Michele Arcangelo a Morfisa. The monastery annexed to the church has

candidates.name: San Gregorio Armeno
candidates.content: The church was completed in 1640, in honor of Saint Gregory of Armenia and it represents, along with the adjacent monastery, one of the most relevant Baroque complexes in Naples. The interior is decorated with 52 frescoes by Luca

candidates.name: Santa Maria del Carmine Maggiore
candidates.content: One of Naples' main churches, related to important historical events of the city and its kingdom, such as Masaniello revolt and the executions happened during the five months existence of Parthenopean Republic (1799). The interior

candidates.name: Castel dell'Ovo
candidates.content: The oldest castle of the city, located on the former island of Megaride, now a peninsula, on the Gulf of Naples. The castle's name comes from a legend that the Roman poet Virgil (who had a reputation in medieval times as a great s

candidates.name: Castel Sant'Elmo
candidates.content: A huge, imposing hilltop medieval fortress, providing outlooks to the surrounding city and hosting a small art gallery. Great place to watch the sunset behind Ischia and Procida.

candidates.name: Naples National Archeological Museum
candidates.alt: Museo archeologico nazionale di Napoli, MANN
candidates.price: €20, free with Artecard and on the first Sunday of month, for visitors below 18 years of age or with disability.
candidates.content: The most important Italian archaeological museum about Roman civilization, it contains a large collection of Roman artifacts from Pompeii, Stabiae and Herculaneum. The collection includes works of the highest quality produced in G

candidates.name: Royal Palace and National Museum of Capodimonte
candidates.price: €10 for adult, €2 for EU citizens aged 18-25, €6.50 after 14:00, free with Artecard.
candidates.content: Hosts paintings from the 13th to 18th centuries, including major works by Simone Martini, Raphael, Titian, Caravaggio, Masaccio, Sandro Botticelli, Lorenzo Lotto, Giovanni Bellini, Giorgio Vasari, El Greco, Jacob Philipp Hackert.

candidates.name: Palazzo delle Arti
candidates.content: A civic museum born as a public exhibition center for the civic collections of arts, and to host art and culture events organized by the City of Naples.

candidates.name: Palazzo Zevallos
candidates.content: Elegant palace built in 1639 by the noble Spanish family Zevallos. It houses a rich art gallery comprising sculptures and paintings from 17th to 19th century, some of them realized by artists of the School of Posillipo.

candidates.name: San Francesco di Paola
candidates.content: One of the main churches in Naples, it's at the west side of Piazza del Plebiscito, the city's main square. The place was planned by King Joachim Murat of Naples (Napoleon's brother-in-law) as a tribute to the emperor. When Napole

candidates.name: Gesù Nuovo
candidates.content: The Church of Gesù Nuovo (New Jesus) was built in 1470 as a palace for Roberto Sanseverino, Prince of Salerno. The Jesuits had already built a church in Naples, now called Gesú Vecchio. Political intrigues caused the property to b

candidates.name: Santa Chiara
candidates.content: A religious complex which includes the Church of Santa Chiara, a monastery, tombs, and an archaeological museum. The double monastic complex was built in 1313-1340 by Queen Sancha of Majorca and her husband King Robert of Naples.

candidates.name: Naples Cathedral
candidates.alt: Duomo di Napoli, Cattedrale di Santa Maria Assunta or Cattedrale di San Gennaro
candidates.content: Built in the 18th century, it is the main church of Naples. It is widely known as the Cattedrale di San Gennaro, in honour of Saint Januarius, the city's patron saint. It was built on the foundations of two palaeo-Christian basili

candidates.name: Castel Nuovo
candidates.content: Often called Maschio Angioino, it is a medieval castle and the main symbol of the architecture of the city. It was first begun in 1279 by Charles I of Anjou and completed three years later. Castel Nuovo soon became the nucleus of

candidates.name: Castel Capuano
candidates.content: The second most ancient castle of Naples after Castel dell'Ovo, built in 12th century by the Normans over a necropolis for use as a royal palace. It was then used as a residence for distinguished visitors such as Francesco Petrarc

candidates.name: Certosa e Museo di San Martino
candidates.content: A former monastery complex, now a museum. It is the most visible landmark of the city, perched atop the Vomero hill that commands the gulf. A Carthusian monastery, it was finished and inaugurated under the rule of Queen Joan I in

candidates.name: Galleria Umberto I
candidates.content: A public shopping gallery that is directly across from the San Carlo opera house. It was designed by Emanuele Rocco, who employed modern architectural elements reminiscent of the Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II in Milan. The Galleri

candidates.name: Catacombe di San Gaudioso
candidates.content: A catacombe area where macabre ritual of "draining" was performed. A few remains of skulls in the walls, parts of skeletons and wall paintings are shown. Also the history of the "upstairs" church is shortly showcased.

candidates.name: Fontana del Gigante
candidates.content: One of the most beautiful fountains of the city, made in the beginning of 17th century by Pietro Bernini, father of the more famous Gian Lorenzo. It was used to sit beside the Royal Palace, close to the statue of a giant. It was t

candidates.name: Museum of Contemporary Art Donnaregina
candidates.content: Very nice museum for contemporary art, with a permanent collection of fascinating, small room installations and temporary exhibitions.

candidates.name: Complesso monumentale dei Girolamini
candidates.price: €5 with reductions, free on first Sunday of the month
candidates.content: Ecclesiastic complex comprising a gallery of paintings, a cloister, a library of thousands of ancient manuscripts, and a baroque church.

candidates.name: National railway Museum of Pietrarsa
candidates.content: A museum housed in the ancient 19th century's Bourbon Factories, along the route of the first railway in Italy: the Napoli-Portici line. Here is possible to admire a large variety of rolling stock like steam locomotives and differ

candidates.name: Museo Universitario delle Scienze e delle Arti
candidates.content: One of the most ancient Anatomy museums of Europe, located in the religious complex of Santa Patrizia, where is possible to discover this fascinating context in the sections of anatomy, pharmacology, stomatology, bibliography and

candidates.name: Royal Palace
candidates.content: One of the four residences used by the Bourbon Kings of Naples during their rule of the Kingdom of Two Sicilies (1730-1860). The Royal Palace is on the site of an earlier building meant to host King Philip III of Spain, who howeve

candidates.name: Albergo dei Poveri
candidates.content: A former public hospital/almshouse. It was designed by the architect Ferdinando Fuga, and construction was started in 1751. It is five storeys tall and about 300 m long. It was popularly known as "Palazzo Fuga". King Charles III o

candidates.name: Palazzo di Sangro di Casacalenda
candidates.content: 3-stores palace built during the second half of 18th century by the architect Mario Gioffredo. The internal courtyard was designed by Luigi Vanvitelli and features a four-arch portico and Doric order lesenes.

candidates.name: Palazzo Mannajuolo
candidates.content: Art Nouveau residential building built in 1911, with an impressive ellipsoidal staircase in marble. The palace is a condo and it is possible to have a look inside asking the doorman

candidates.name: Accordi @ Disaccordi - International Short Film Festival
candidates.content: If you are in Naples during the summer, you can experience the cinema beneath the stars on warm nights, in an amphiteatre equipped with one of the widest projection screens in Italy which rises having an artificial lake all around

candidates.name: Pontile di Bagnoli
candidates.content: A walk of 900 m (½ mile) suspended on the waters of the Gulf of Pozzuoli, along a concrete pier built in 1962 to serve a former steel mill, closed in 1993 and now dismantled. Enjoy a relaxing stroll surrounded by the stunning view

candidates.name: Real Teatro San Carlo
candidates.content: Founded in 1737, is the oldest continuously active opera house in Europe. In the 18th century, Naples was the capital of European music, and even foreign composers like Hasse, Haydn, Johann Christian Bach and Gluck considered the

candidates.name: Teatro Bellini
candidates.content: Built in 1878 and named after the Sicilian composer Vincenzo Bellini, the Bellini Theatre hosted prestigious events such as operas for almost a century. In 1960s a period of decline started for the structure, that became a sort of

candidates.name: Underwater Park of Gaiola
candidates.content: Diving, snorkelling or trip on glass-bottomed boat "Aquavision" in the marine protected area of the minor island of Gaiola, off Posillipo elegant quarter. Just choose your favourite way to discover this stretch of coastline and th

candidates.name: Teatro Augusteo
candidates.content: A theatre designed by Pier Luigi Nervi in 1929 and built inside an 18th-century noble palace, along the central Via Toledo. The structure was closed during World War II and reopened during 1950s as a cinema, until it was finally r

candidates.name: Centro Sub Campi Flegrei
candidates.content: A 5*IDC diving centre offering diving and snorkelling in the Gulf of Naples, around the Phlegraean islands and within the underwater Archaeological Park of Baiae (the so-called submerged Pompeii!) Open all year.

candidates.name: Gran Caffè Gambrinus
candidates.content: Enjoy the special Neapolitan coffee in one of the most prestigious and famous cafes in Italy. Founded in 1860 in the rear of Palazzo delle Prefettura, the cafe was also known for being a meeting site for intellectuals, artists and

candidates.name: Bar Mexico
candidates.content: One of the best coffees you can enjoy in the city, just 50 metres away from central railway station.

candidates.name: Bar Salvo
candidates.content: Great coffee and pastries in an informal cafe along a pedestrian area in the elegant Vomero quarter.

candidates.name: Enoteca Belledonne
candidates.content: Taste the best Italian wines along with cheeses, hams, sausages and pastries in an elegant wine bar and shop in Chiaia district.

candidates.name: Il Mantegno
candidates.content: Great wines, cocktails, beer and appetizers in a small but nice wine bar in the historic centre.

candidates.name: Mosto
candidates.content: Excellent selection of beer and cocktails in a beautiful pub with jazz music.

candidates.name: Spuzzulè Winebar
candidates.content: Wide choice of wines accompanied by typical regional dishes.

candidates.name: Archeobar
candidates.content: Specialises in Negronis

candidates.name: Arenile di Bagnoli
candidates.content: Beach club with pool and solarium by day, vibrant disco by night. Various live performances of international DJs.

candidates.name: Riva Club
candidates.content: Seaside disco with an elegant and modern atmosphere, located in front of the island of Nisida.

candidates.name: Virgilio Club
candidates.content: Live music and excellent drinks in the enchanting location of Posillipo, overlooking the bay.

candidates.name: Caffè Ciorfito
candidates.content: Taste the authentic Neapolitan coffee and pastries in a welcoming cafe in the heart of the old town, usually visited by Italian actors.

candidates.name: L'Antica Pizzeria da Michele
candidates.content: Pizza Margherita with a crust which is both thin and chewy. There is usually a queue. Get a numbered ticket from the waiter at the door when you arrive, then wait outside for your number to be called. The pizzas are cooked quickly

candidates.name: Di Matteo
candidates.content: Il presidente, Sorbillo, and his sister, a few doors away (informally known as "la vecchia", the old lady, from the owner of the pizzeria, a very small place with only 4 or 5 tables, that looks like a pizzeria of 50 years ago - ve

candidates.name: Trattoria da Peppino Ritrovo degli Artisti
candidates.content: Simple family restaurant where the owner, Raffaele Liguori, will provide you with local Neapolitan dishes at low prices. Few tables, booking recommended.

candidates.name: Pizzoteca Quartiere Spagnoli
candidates.content: Good vibes and pizzas for an affordable price.

candidates.name: Trattoria Don Vincenzo
candidates.content: Wide choice of dishes in the middle of the old town.

candidates.name: Decumano 31
candidates.content: Regional street food in a street with character. Here you can try the Neapolitan frittini.

candidates.name: 120 Grammi Spaghetti Takeaway
candidates.content: It's a combination of street food and pasta, with an intense taste: you can choose between a variety of spices.

candidates.name: Il Cuoppo
candidates.content: Hole in the wall spot for fried snacks. It's a small eatery for seafood, mozzarella balls, fried zucchini blossoms and anchovies to go.

candidates.name: Pizzeria Trianon
candidates.content: The pizzas are less soupy and with crispier crusts.

candidates.name: Drago d'Oro
candidates.content: Asian cuisine in a cheap and informal Chinese restaurant close to Via Toledo.

candidates.name: Pasticceria Poppella
candidates.content: An incredible choice of the best traditional pastries. There is another location in Via Arena alla Sanità, 28 near Palazzo dello Spagnolo.

candidates.name: Sfogliatella Mary
candidates.content: A small pastry shop become a sort of "must-see" for tourists, due to the quality of its Neapolitan pastries, especially the sfogliatelle.

Neapolitan cuisine in general features much seafood, befitting its status as an ancient and still functioning port. The most popular fish recipe is Polpo alla lucìana, consisting in octopus cooked in a terracotta pan with tomatoes, garlic, capers, pepper and black olives of Gaeta, served with chopped parsley.
